scope: Theorem 2.3 (Moment-graph sheaf) of the manuscript “Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials” (preprints/Combinatorial-Invariance-of-Kazhdan-Lusztig-Polynomials-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 168 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7e1be2107a85e28d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an indecomposable graded sheaf B = B(b) on [1, b], normalized by Bb = A, with the following properties. 1. Every vertex module Bx is finitely generated and graded free. For E : x −→ y, BE = By /αEBy , and restriction from y is the quotient map. 2. If Ω ⊆ [1, b] is upward closed, every section over Ω extends to a global section. Moreover the projection from global sections onto each Bx is surjective. 3. Let Ux be the set of edges out of x. For F ⊆ Ux put Lx(F) = ker Bx −→ M E∈F BE ! . Then Lx(Ux) is graded free.
